claims.text: Arc melting on a water-cooled copper hearth provides rapid quenching relative to conventional slower-cooling synthesis.
Rapid quenching can kinetically retain a metastable microstructure in an almost equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy.
Rapid quenching produces a defect-rich microstructure.
The kinetically trapped microstructure has finer grains than a slowly cooled comparator.
The kinetically trapped microstructure has increased defect density relative to a slowly cooled comparator.
Rapid quenching may retain metastable phase regions.
Grain boundaries, dislocations, and metastable microstructural inhomogeneities act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Increased domain-wall pinning raises coercivity by obstructing magnetic-domain movement.
Rapid quenching prevents or limits equilibration during synthesis.
Rapid quenching hinders the formation of soft, fully ordered ferromagnetic phases.
A rapidly quenched FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy will have higher coercivity than a compositionally matched, more slowly cooled alloy.
Conventionally cooled or C14 Laves-dominant FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys exhibit soft ferromagnetism with lower coercivity.
Slower cooling promotes a C14 Laves-dominant phase in the proposed compositionally matched comparator.
If the cooling rate is insufficient to suppress equilibrium phase formation, the coercivity enhancement will diminish.
